correctness.rationale: Exact bilateral resolvent kernel follows by rational partial fractions and a Green jump equation, with absolute summability and unit mass. Difference commutation plus a Heaviside jump proves the sharp BV norm. Complex phase ensures negative coefficients at every positive strength. The Banach-algebra Neumann expansion yields 1+4λ+O(λ²); an exponentially dominated lattice-to-continuum Riemann sum yields the stated closed limit and first-negative-index scaling. A standalone exact-rational radius-7 finite-section certificate bounds two infinite norms and proves a nonmonotone parameter pair without floating-point assumptions. All formulas and normalization were independently reconstructed and the checker executed.

value.rationale: The exact sharp gain quantifies edge-ringing amplification of the classical low-pass smoothing resolvent on bounded variation signals. A step waveform is a universal worst-case witness, every positive strength violates variation contraction, the gain is rigorously nonmonotone and the large-smoothing limit has a nontrivial exact constant 1.140093467..., despite increasing smoothing scale. This directly distinguishes spectral damping from BV stability and supplies a reusable sharp all-parameter bound, not a routine special parameter computation.
